function.name: lawsuit_search

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Reference Guide** | Topic | Key Points | Where to Find More | |-------|------------|--------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits are the law.
• 55 mph on rural interstates, 65 mph on urban interstates, 45 mph on most rural roads, 35 mph on most urban roads.
• School zones: 25 mph (or 20 mph if posted). | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑Safety** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child‑safety seat or booster.
• No “seat‑belt law” for adults in Texas, but failure to buckle can lead to a fine if the driver is pulled over. | Texas Transportation Code §545.002 | | **Cell‑Phone Use** | • Hand‑held use is prohibited while driving.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed.
• Texting while driving is illegal. | Texas Transportation Code §545.003 | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08 % or higher is illegal.
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21 (0.02 % BAC). | Texas Transportation Code §545.004 | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Yield to pedestrians at crosswalks.
• Stop at stop signs and red lights.
• “Yield” signs require giving way to traffic already in the intersection. | Texas Transportation Code §545.005 | | **School Bus** | • Stop for a school bus with its stop sign extended and lights flashing.
• Vehicles must stop on both sides of the road. | Texas Transportation Code §545.006 | | **Lane‑Changing & Overtaking** | • Use turn signals.
• Do not cut off other drivers.
• “Lane‑change” violations can result in a fine. | Texas Transportation Code §545.007 | | **Parking** | • No parking in front of driveways, fire hydrants, or on sidewalks.
• Parking in a “no parking” zone is a ticket. | Texas Transportation Code §545.008 | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • All vehicles must be registered and display a valid license plate.
• Most vehicles must pass an annual safety inspection. | Texas Transportation Code §545.009 | | **Insurance** | • Minimum liability coverage: $30,000 for bodily injury per person, $60,000 for bodily injury per accident, $25,000 for property damage. | Texas Transportation Code §545.010 | | **Special Situations** | • **Towing**: Must use a tow bar or chain; cannot tow a vehicle that is not in motion.
• **Motorcycles**: Must wear a helmet (unless under 18).
• **Commercial Vehicles**: Additional regulations for trucks and buses. | Texas Transportation Code §§545.011–545.020 | --- ### How to Stay Updated 1. **Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT)** – Official website: [https://www.txdot.gov](https://www.txdot.gov) 2. **Texas Transportation Code** – Accessible via the Texas Legislature’s website: [https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov](https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov) 3. **Local County Courts** – For specific enforcement actions or recent changes. --- ### Quick Tips for Safe Driving in Texas - **Always obey posted speed limits** – they’re set for safety. - **Keep your seat belt fastened** – it’s a simple habit that saves lives. - **Avoid distractions** – especially texting or using a phone while driving. - **Check your insurance** – make sure you’re covered at or above the state minimum. - **Stay alert at school zones** – speeds drop significantly, and children are present. --- #### Need More Detail? If you’re looking for specific statutes, recent court cases, or want to know how a particular law applies to a unique situation (e.g., a new technology like autonomous vehicles), let me know! I can pull up the exact legal text or summarize relevant case law.
